title: Small-business owners protest COVID-19 closure measures
location: Outside the Kuwait Lawyers Society, after security prevented a gathering outside the National Assembly
scope: One reported gathering of salon, barbershop, and health-club owners; no multi-city or broader-series scope is established.
participants_original: The article describes dozens of salon, barbershop, and health-club owners; it gives no numeric count.
threshold_50_evidence: The qualitative term “dozens” is not a reliable numeric minimum of 50. Attendance bounds are unknown; eligibility remains pending_threshold.

title.summary: The opened Kuwait Times report describes business owners protesting announced COVID-19 business closures.

start_date.summary: The article is stamped 6 February 2021 at 10:46 p.m. EDT; its body/image caption says the protest was yesterday. Converting that timestamp to Kuwait local time places publication on 7 February, so yesterday is interpreted as 6 February Kuwait time; this is an explicit timezone-based inference.

end_date.summary: The article reports a move from the National Assembly area to the Lawyers Society but no event closure or end date.

location.summary: The report says security prevented a gathering outside the National Assembly and owners then protested outside the Kuwait Lawyers Society.

scope.summary: One protest by dozens of owners is reported; no larger campaign, additional site, or separate action is established by the read.

organizer.summary: The report mentions small-business representatives but does not name an organizer for the protest.

demands.summary: Owners urged authorities to stop implementing measures that shut salons, barbershops, and health clubs; coded as social restrictions.

participants_original.summary: The report uses “dozens” for salon, barbershop, and health-club owners; no numeric turnout is given.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: “Dozens” does not establish at least 50 people; numeric bounds remain null.

protester_violence.summary: The article does not explicitly establish protester violence or its absence; code unknown.

state_response.summary: Security prevented gathering at the Assembly site before protesters moved, supporting crowd_dispersal=yes. The speaker reported that the prime minister agreed to reconsider measures and a committee meeting with representatives was planned, supporting accommodation=yes as receipt/review of demands, not a policy victory. Arrests, beatings, ignore, killings, and shootings are not established and remain unknown.

notes: The article reports an actual gathering, but “dozens” does not establish the dataset’s 50-person threshold. The prime minister’s reported agreement was to reconsider measures; a final policy outcome is not documented. Do not merge with the separately planned Feb. 5 Salons Union sit-in (E002) without further evidence.
open_questions: Can a contemporaneous source establish a numeric attendance estimate of at least 50?
Was a named union or association the organizer?
What exact time did the gathering begin and end?
Was the prime minister’s review directly prompted by this gathering, and what policy outcome followed?
Is this distinct from the planned Salons Union sit-in reported for Feb. 5?
